row.bound_formula: Horner over a field F on L words (L-1 degree, unblinded): eps(L) = (L-1)/|F| = (L-1)/2^64 for GF(2^64) (Bernstein: n/#k for n components in the s-blinded degree-n authenticator; paper: (2n-1)/2^64 on 2n words) -> bits = min_L log2(L/eps) = 64. BRW on n words: eps(n) = (2n-1)/2^64 for fixed n >= 1 (Bernstein Sec. 5.7); variable length only with the S-restriction of Theorem 5.6 (or a length prefix) -> bits = min_n log2(n·2^64/(2n-1)) -> 63 (table entry 63). SMHasher3 poly-mersenne (code claim): eps = len/p, p = 2^61-1, len = number of 32-bit characters incl. the length character (ceil(bytes/4)+1); strictly the key a is drawn from [0,(p-1)/2) so Schwartz–Zippel gives len/2^60, and the 32-bit output adds ~2^-32 (plus, for deg0, the wrap effect 2^32/(2^61-1) = 2^-29 measured in the paper's appendix). Paper F_{2^89-1} row: p = 2^89-1, three-key bound n/p on 2n words, single-key (3n-1)/p; the table's 88 bits equals min_n log2(2n·2^89/(3n-1)) ≈ 88.4 (the n/p form would give 89); the timed two-key harness form's comment states (N+2)/2^63 with y drawn from 2^63 values. Harness Mersenne 2^89-1 Horner (not a table row): (words-1)·2^25/p ≈ words/2^64 with 64-bit truncated output.
row.proved_vs_assumed: PROVED (Horner, BRW, Bernstein): information-theoretic, for r, s "independent uniform random elements of k" hidden from the attacker, messages chosen independently of the key; no computational or independence assumption beyond the uniform key; fixed length n per bound, variable length for BRW only via Theorem 5.6's alphabet restriction (0 ∉ S, S ∩ (S+1) = ∅). The paper's framework rows draw the key uniformly per call (getRandomUInt64) and hash fixed-length messages, matching the theorem. PROVED (paper's F_{2^89-1} row): Schwartz–Zippel over uniform keys in F_p; caveat from the paper (injective.tex:294-298 and appendix "Truncated Mersenne outputs"): "the low $64$ bits of an $89$-bit Mersenne residue are \emph{not} a safe output: a pair differing by $2^{64}-1$ in the last word collides with probability $2^{-25}$, so the Mersenne rows output the full residue" — yet the harness struct that produced the timings (PaperMers89Smart) returns (uint64_t)m89_reduce(P), the low 64 bits, and draws y from [0,2^63) not [0,p); the throughput is unaffected (a cast) but the 88-bit score presumes the full residue and field-uniform keys. ASSUMED / NOT COVERED (SMHasher3 poly-mersenne): the len/p claim is a code comment, not a published theorem; the key a and the finalizer coefficients are derived from a 64-bit seed with splitmix ("Hash quality is dependent on the RNG used! If you plan on using this hash, it is STRONGLY recommended that you test it with the RNG you plan on using to seed it."), i.e. a 2^64-member subfamily, not a uniform field element; a is restricted to < (p-1)/2 for lazy reduction; output truncated to 32 of 61 bits; the Ahle–Knudsen–Thorup paper proves k-universality of single-word polynomial hashing (Definition 1; eq. (4) collision probability (1 + (r-1)/p^2)/r after bit selection), not the string hash. The "K-independence" claimed by the finalizer comment holds for the finalizer as a map of the 61-bit residue, not for the composed string hash.
row.key_words: Horner F_2^64: 1; Horner unrolled: 1 (x^2, x^4 recomputed per call); BRW: 1 (the lg n squarings r^2, r^4, ... are recomputed per call; Bernstein Sec. 5.8: "One could cache r2 , r4 , r8 , . . ., eliminating the squarings in favor of lg n variables."); paper F_{2^89-1} row: 5 as printed in the table (harness: x in [0,p) = 2 words, x^2 = 2 words, y = 1 word); SMHasher3 poly-mersenne.degK: 1 word a (< 2^60) + (K+1) finalizer words poly_mersenne_random[0..K] (a second word b is drawn but never used): deg0 1, deg1 3, deg2 4, deg3 5, deg4 6 — all derived from one 64-bit seed; harness Mersenne 2^89-1 Horner: 1 (64-bit x).
row.output_bits: Horner / Horner unrolled / BRW over GF(2^64): 64. Paper F_{2^89-1} row: 89 as printed ("(89-bit output)"); the timed harness code returns the low 64 bits. SMHasher3 poly-mersenne.deg0..4: 32 ($.bits = 32; memcpy(out, &h, 4) of a 61-bit residue). Harness Mersenne 2^89-1 Horner: 64 (truncated).

No maintained standalone BRW library was located; the paper cites Chakraborty et al. (hardware) and Ghosh–Sarkar (software) for other BRW implementations. Bernstein, "Polynomial evaluation and message authentication", manuscript dated 2007.10.22, 14 pp. (typeset for Contemporary Mathematics; never formally published), https://cr.yp.to/papers.html#pema, PDF https://cr.yp.to/antiforgery/pema-20071022.pdf — the paper's bib key is Bernstein:2011:RW with year 2007. row.notes: (1) Three distinct objects share this family: Bernstein's proofs cover Horner and BRW for a uniform field key; the SMHasher3 poly-mersenne hash has only a code-comment bound (len/p) and is credited to Ahle 2020, whose paper proves single-word k-universal hashing (data = evaluation point), not a string hash — do not cite arXiv:2008.08654 as the proof of the poly-mersenne string bound. (2) BRW scores 63 rather than 64 because its bound is (2n-1)/2^64; its injectivity (Bernstein Thm 5.5) gives an almost-universal "authenticator", not k-independence; the paper's related-work text insists on the injective (BRW) vs bijective (Rabin–Winograd) distinction. (3) Inconsistency worth flagging for the F_{2^89-1} row: the table says "(89-bit output)", key 5, 88 bits, and the appendix says the Mersenne rows "output the full residue", but the harness struct that produced 4.4/3.9 GB/s (PaperMers89Smart) returns the low 64 bits of the residue and draws y from 2^63 values (its own comment bounds Pr[coll] by (N+2)/2^63); throughput is the same either way, but the 88-bit score presumes the full-residue, field-uniform-key version. 88 matches min_n log2(2n·2^89/(3n-1)) (single-key bound), not n/p (which gives 89). (4) SMHasher3 poly-mersenne processes 4 bytes per 64x64 multiply, hence the 0.50 bytes/cycle bulk figure; it is FLAG_IMPL_SLOW (bulk runs/trials ÷4, SeedDifferential run at 2^20 seeds, extra tiers skipped; the paper's appendix notes "Hashes that SMHasher3 registers as slow implementations (SipHash, the Mersenne polynomial hash, HighwayHash) run only the default tier, scaled down to $2^{20}$ seeds ... and pass it"). deg1/deg2 fail many distribution tests because a degree-1/2 finalizer on a 32-bit truncation is too weak, not because the collision bound fails; deg3/deg4 pass 238/238. (5) Release attribution for the SMHasher3 numbers is inferred from the raw files' last-regeneration commit (ea0b94f9, 2025-10-16) matching 20251015-release-5035a923; the README footer only says one of three releases. (6) rurban's table row for poly_1_mersenne reads "fails most tests"; rurban's numbers are on an AMD Ryzen 5 3350G 3.6GHz (MiB/sec = bulk 262144-byte keys, cycl./hash = 1-31 byte keys), older code (srand-seeded, h = len_bytes ^ seed). (7) The paper's Horner/BRW rows are fixed-length framework benchmarks (message length is a template parameter), so the variable-length caveat of BRW (Bernstein Thm 5.6) does not arise there; a length prefix would be needed in practice. (8) An earlier pass had already written excerpts.md in the same scratchpad directory; this pass re-downloaded every source and re-verified each quote (verified_excerpts_pass2.md carries the fresh line numbers, which differ from the earlier pema.txt/ahle2020.txt copies only by file name).

reference: the arXiv listing and the PDF byline read "Jakob Tejs Bæk Knudsen", not "Jakob Bæk Tejs Knudsen".

proved_vs_assumed: the framework rows do NOT draw the key per call. tools/bench/adversarial/speed.cpp row<>() (line 118) calls h.seed(sr) once per row; FW::seed() (speed_hashes.h:282) runs c.init(), where getRandomUInt64 fills the MESSAGE words (injective_hashing_arm.h:261, 374), and draws x = r.next() once; every timed call is c(x) with the same key and message. The key is uniform but fixed for the whole row.

bound_formula: "(the n/p form would give 89)" is wrong: the three-key n/|F| bound on 2n words gives log2(2n·2^89/n) = 90. The attribution of 88 to the single-key bound is also under-determined: the timed two-key harness form with y uniform in F_p gives min_N log2((15N/8)·2^89/(N+2)) = 88.32 at N=1, i.e. also 88; with y drawn from [0,2^63) as coded, the harness's own comment bound (N+2)/2^63 yields about 62.3 bits.

The SpeedTest.cpp:263-264 bulk ÷4 and the extra-tier isSlow() skips ARE upstream (Wojcik, 2023). The appendix sentence about slow hashes and 2^20 seeds therefore describes the author's fork, and the record should say so.
